claims.citation: New York Herald, 30 September 1866, p. 8, col. 4
claims.verbatim:
Ship Eugenie (Ham), Cahubley[?], Hamburg, 39 days, with
mdse and 300 passengers, to R M Sloman & Edye. Sept 22,
20 miles SSE from Sable Island, encountered a hurricane,
beginning at SE and going completely around the compass;
was obliged to cut away all three topgallantmasts, and in
falling they carried away the foretopmast. Sept 1, lat 53 35,
lon 19, saw a bark, showing a white signal, with red cross,
and letters D P in it, standing E; 11th, lat 46 12, lon 41 20,
spoke ship Wm Sturges, from St John, NB, for Liverpool;
12th, lat 45 22, lon 41 51, ship Herzogin von Brabant (Brem),
from Bremen for New York, 30 days out; 13th, lat 40 40, lon
42 57, bark Herald (Br), 26 days from Whitehaven for Que-
bec; 15th, lat 44 58, lon 44 51, bark Laura (Brem), 30 days
from Bremen for New York; same day, ship Napoleon
(Norw), from Bermuda for Antwerp.
